drills.title: U10 PLAY · WIDE | Draw, pass, use the edge
drills.players: Eight attackers (A1–A8) and eight defenders (D1–D8) on a regulation-size U10 diagram. Rotate roles. Use a smaller marked area for walk-throughs.
drills.equipment: One size-4 rugby ball; 4+ cones for the optional reduced practice area.
drills.objective: Fix a defender, make legal backward passes to deep outside receivers, and attack space on the edge.
drills.coaching: Run straight before passing. Supporters stay behind the passer. If the defender holds width, carry into the available inside channel.
drills.safety: Animated tactical illustration, not a contact technique lesson. Walk through with non-contact opposition first. All match play must follow current RFU U10 rules; no obstruction, forward passing or dangerous contact.
drills.instructions: Call WIDE. A2 fixes D3, passes to deeper A3; A3 straightens at D4 and passes to deeper A4. A4 accelerates with A3 and A5 in support.
drills.regression: Walk through with four key players, then repeat with the full 8-a-side line against passive opposition.
drills.progression: Let defenders react naturally. Keep possession if the expected gap does not appear; the call is a decision cue, not a compulsory scripted pass.
drills.questions: Did A2 fix D3? Were both passes backwards? When should the carrier hold the ball?
drills.notes: Match-day code: WIDE. This editable Classic drill shows a proposed attacking/defensive picture, not a guaranteed match outcome. Use action camera to zoom into the relevant players. Ruckus mode shares the same movement data. Contact coaching must be taught separately.

frames.name: WIDE · set up the shape
frames.notes: A2 starts with the ball; A3 and A4 are deeper and wider.

frames.name: Go straight · draw D3
frames.notes: A2 fixes D3 by running square towards the defender; A3 holds support depth.

frames.name: Pass behind · A3 receives
frames.notes: A2 passes backwards to A3 after D3 has committed.

frames.name: A3 straightens at D4
frames.notes: A3 goes forward and fixes D4; A4 continues wider, behind the ball.

frames.name: Pass backwards · A4 outside
frames.notes: A3 passes backwards to A4, outside the second defender.

frames.name: A4 exploits edge
frames.notes: A4 accelerates in the edge channel while A3 and A5 support.

frames.name: Review · pass or keep?
frames.notes: If the defenders hold outside, keep the ball and attack inside instead of forcing the pass.

drills.title: U10 PLAY · SWITCH | Sell outside, attack inside
drills.players: Eight attackers (A1–A8) and eight defenders (D1–D8) on a regulation-size U10 diagram. Rotate roles. Use a smaller marked area for walk-throughs.
drills.equipment: One size-4 rugby ball; 4+ cones for the optional reduced practice area.
drills.objective: Create an inside gap with a legal switch pass to a deeper supporting player.
drills.coaching: A3 sells an outside carry. A4 starts behind and curves inside behind the carrier, not across a defender. Keep the pass backwards and don't obstruct.
drills.safety: Animated tactical illustration, not a contact technique lesson. Walk through with non-contact opposition first. All match play must follow current RFU U10 rules; no obstruction, forward passing or dangerous contact.
drills.instructions: Call SWITCH. A3 draws D4 towards the touchline, A4 cuts behind and back inside. A3 makes a backward switch pass; A4 straightens. Only use it if the inside channel opens.
drills.regression: Walk through with four key players, then repeat with the full 8-a-side line against passive opposition.
drills.progression: Let defenders react naturally. Keep possession if the expected gap does not appear; the call is a decision cue, not a compulsory scripted pass.
drills.questions: Was A4 behind at the pass? Why must A4 run behind A3? What if D4 stays inside?
drills.notes: Match-day code: SWITCH. This editable Classic drill shows a proposed attacking/defensive picture, not a guaranteed match outcome. Use action camera to zoom into the relevant players. Ruckus mode shares the same movement data. Contact coaching must be taught separately.

frames.name: SWITCH · A3 carries, A4 stays deep
frames.notes: A3 will sell an outside line; A4 is behind and outside ready to return inside.

frames.name: A3 tempts D4 to drift outside
frames.notes: A3 runs towards D4's outside shoulder. A4 curves behind the carrier.

frames.name: Switch pass · A4 runs inside
frames.notes: A4 runs BEHIND A3, not across the defender's path. A3 passes backwards at release.

frames.name: A4 straightens into the gap
frames.notes: A4 runs square and attacks space inside D4; A3 becomes support.

frames.name: A4 attacks, A3 supports
frames.notes: The pass was behind; the receiver accelerates into space rather than running around a blocking team-mate.

frames.name: Review · only if the gap opens
frames.notes: Never force the switch when the defender stays inside; a normal support pass or carry may be better.

drills.title: U10 PLAY · GO AGAIN | Win the next phase
drills.players: Eight attackers (A1–A8) and eight defenders (D1–D8) on a regulation-size U10 diagram. Rotate roles. Use a smaller marked area for walk-throughs.
drills.equipment: One size-4 rugby ball; 4+ cones for the optional reduced practice area.
drills.objective: Tackle, release, present, one-per-side ruck support, secure the ball and pass away quickly to a new runner.
drills.coaching: Tackler releases; grounded carrier presents back. Only one additional on-feet player from each side joins. Others stay onside. When available, move the ball away promptly.
drills.safety: Animated tactical illustration, not a contact technique lesson. Walk through with non-contact opposition first. All match play must follow current RFU U10 rules; no obstruction, forward passing or dangerous contact. Only one extra on-feet player per team joins the tackle participants to form a U10 ruck. Contact under qualified coach supervision.
drills.instructions: Call GO AGAIN. A2 takes contact from D3, presents back after the release; A3 and D4 form the limited U10 ruck. A1 collects available ball and passes behind to A4, who attacks a new channel.
drills.regression: Start with two-handed touch, simulated presentation and stationary, non-contact ruck participants. Full contact only with a qualified age-grade coach.
drills.progression: Let defenders react naturally. Keep possession if the expected gap does not appear; the call is a decision cue, not a compulsory scripted pass.
drills.questions: How many additional players per side? Who releases? Who picks up after a formed ruck? How soon must the ball be played?
drills.notes: Match-day code: GO AGAIN. This editable Classic drill shows a proposed attacking/defensive picture, not a guaranteed match outcome. Use action camera to zoom into the relevant players. Ruckus mode shares the same movement data. Contact coaching must be taught separately.

frames.name: GO AGAIN · A2 has the ball
frames.notes: A2 carries with A1 and A3 in support; A4 waits deeper for the next phase.

frames.name: Go forward · support follows
frames.notes: A2 attacks space, A3 supports, D3 tracks the carrier.

frames.name: Controlled tackle · A2 to ground
frames.notes: D3 performs a qualified-coach-supervised U10 tackle; sequence only, not technique.

frames.name: Release and present back
frames.notes: D3 releases and clears. A2 presents the ball on the attacking side.

frames.name: A3 and D4 approach on feet
frames.notes: Only the one additional player per side joins the tackle participants at the U10 ruck.

frames.name: Ruck · one arriving player each
frames.notes: A3 and D4 engage over the ball, with all other players behind their team's offside line.

frames.name: Contest · possession secured
frames.notes: Both on-feet players remain engaged; A3 secures possession and no extra players join.

frames.name: A1 retrieves available ball
frames.notes: A1 takes the available ball from behind the ruck and prepares to pass it away promptly.

frames.name: Pass behind · A4 receives
frames.notes: A1 passes backwards to A4, who stays deeper and outside the previous tackle.

frames.name: A4 attacks the next channel
frames.notes: A4 attacks space, rather than crowding the previous contact, with A5 in support.

frames.name: Review · present, secure, move
frames.notes: Point out release, offside, the limited U10 ruck numbers and playing the ball away.

drills.title: U10 PLAY · WALL | Slide and defend together
drills.players: Eight attackers (A1–A8) and eight defenders (D1–D8) on a regulation-size U10 diagram. Rotate roles. Use a smaller marked area for walk-throughs.
drills.equipment: One size-4 rugby ball; 4+ cones for the optional reduced practice area.
drills.objective: Keep the eight defenders in a connected line and slide together as the attack changes direction.
drills.coaching: Use short calls: WALL, BALL, INSIDE, OUTSIDE. Nearest defender tracks the carrier; neighbours cover gaps and remain connected.
drills.safety: Animated tactical illustration, not a contact technique lesson. Walk through with non-contact opposition first. All match play must follow current RFU U10 rules; no obstruction, forward passing or dangerous contact.
drills.instructions: Call WALL on defence. Begin connected; when A3 passes to A4, move as a line, let D5 take the carrier and D4/D6 cover inside and outside. Start with a controlled two-handed touch, not live tackling.
drills.regression: Walk the defence in a line with a passive attack; use touch only before adding any qualified-coach-supervised legal tackles.
drills.progression: Let defenders react naturally. Keep possession if the expected gap does not appear; the call is a decision cue, not a compulsory scripted pass.
drills.questions: What did the defence do? Was the pass backwards? Who supported the carrier? When should the team keep the ball?
drills.notes: Match-day code: WALL. This editable Classic drill shows a proposed attacking/defensive picture, not a guaranteed match outcome. Use action camera to zoom into the relevant players. Ruckus mode shares the same movement data. Contact coaching must be taught separately.

frames.name: WALL · defenders spread and connect
frames.notes: Defenders establish an even line across the pitch; A3 carries in attack.

frames.name: Move forward together
frames.notes: The defending line moves forward together and scans the ball. No lone defender races ahead.

frames.name: A3 passes wide to A4
frames.notes: A3 makes a backward pass to A4. Defenders slide together towards the new ball carrier.

frames.name: D5 takes ball, neighbours cover
frames.notes: D5 tracks A4; D4 protects inside and D6 covers outside. Keep the line connected.

frames.name: Close safely without gaps
frames.notes: D5 reaches a controlled two-handed touch for this walk-through; match tackling must follow U10 rules.

frames.name: Reset the defensive picture
frames.notes: After the stop, reorganise the defensive line instead of swarming the contact point.

frames.name: Review · defend as one team
frames.notes: Ask: who has the carrier, who covers inside and outside, and where would a gap appear?
